title: November 8: growing rails, timing communication and causal reductions
summary: User's November 8 activity tally: 15 commits across six repositories; five newly indexed repositories, plus one previously inventoried historical ECG repository promoted to reviewed status. Source-reported numerical claims are distinguished from independent test execution.

nodes.claim: v2-v5 rotating train-yard input sampler; vector AIS computes phase-coded XOR under balanced conditions, while a separate pilot entrains listeners and v5 measures timing windows and path sums.
nodes.survived: Source reports 1.44 extra bits from phase release beyond scalar count (no jitter); pilot locking tolerates 32/32 common-delay conditions against 4/32 unlocked. V5 documents phase-window/jitter tradeoff, classical phasor sums and 19 Node tests.
nodes.killed: Private data jitter is not removed by pilot locking. The device is a designed mathematical toy, not a biological neuron, quantum path integral, shortest-route solver or trained neural network.
nodes.era: November 8: phase trains and growing rails

nodes.claim: Independent nine-yard three-layer graph with local clocks, vertical and lateral packets, apical modulatory input, basket-style soma shunt and chandelier-style AIS veto.
nodes.survived: Source reports 30/30 apical-enabled exits vs 0/30 basal alone; basket reduces 1.5 load to 0.3699; chandelier holds 1.5 load while preventing exit. All-yard test gives 72 exits vs 31 with vertical wiring removed.
nodes.killed: Its topology, route types and biological labels are hand-supplied. Not realistic neurons or proof of AI superiority; it has no learned growing tracks.
nodes.era: November 8: phase trains and growing rails

nodes.claim: Sol's independent deterministic phase-gated growing rails: every possible lattice edge receives an exploratory wavefront, a target ACK reinforces the predecessor route, and a 15-unit global material budget makes rails compete.
nodes.survived: On one constructed 12x7 landscape, source reports 73-tick phase-aware delivery vs 94 flow-only; after severing a rail it rebuilds an 80-tick route, and after retargeting gets 78 ticks vs 118 flow-only. Eleven tests and passing Actions reported.
nodes.killed: The explorer is a time-dependent shortest-arrival scheduler with path traceback, not a demonstrated purely local growing organism. Budget and target are global/external. One scenario; not a general TSP solution.
nodes.era: November 8: phase trains and growing rails

nodes.claim: Claude's independent stochastic ant-colony-like walkers, phase-window target reply, budgeted material and evaporating rail strengths in 20 constructed 7x7 worlds.
nodes.survived: Time-aware walker succeeds 14/20 timing-window worlds vs 5/20 time-blind flow and 1/20 Physarum, after cut 13/20 and after retargeting 19/20. Physarum finds optimum 20/20 on the plain shortest-route task.
nodes.killed: The worlds are intentionally constructed so cheapest routes miss the timing window. ACK remembers the walk, the resource budget is nonlocal, and the default strong-feedback learner stays on a bad head-start route or fails in 15/20 worlds.
nodes.era: November 8: phase trains and growing rails

nodes.claim: No-graph-symmetry example of boundary-indistinguishable interior graph *parameters*; a privileged clamped interior key can decode which hidden realization is present.
nodes.survived: Source reports 9-dimensional hidden fiber, 64 keyed words, safe boundary-only plasticity and common hidden scaling. November 8 correction finds that many apparently erased words were merely misread by an out-of-date codebook.
nodes.killed: The storage is parameter nonidentifiability, not a dark dynamical state. Maps between hidden words do not compose, so torsion-freeness is not earned. Interior key/clamp is privileged, and arbitrary plasticity leaks/collapses information.
nodes.era: November 8: phase trains and growing rails

nodes.claim: Causal reduction of the old PerceptionLab image-to-feedback ECG-like controller: 256x256 image branch replaced by a one-dimensional lookup, with ordered 50-sample controller history and four-tick host scheduler.
nodes.survived: Source reports bit-exact reduced trajectory over 3000 ticks; faithful host period 59 instead of the old 52 from a one-tick reconstruction. Clamp and sample-window permutation alter the dynamics; integral_state is updated but never read.
nodes.killed: The four output wires were image samples, not eigenmodes; the large image did not constitute high-dimensional autonomous state, and the 52-tick interpretation was not the faithful host loop.

edges.why: The historical ECG graph and node implementations were frozen in the audit for an exact causal reduction.
Friday's mirror-protected dark sector inspired a distinct non-symmetry parameter fiber; no direct code ancestry or same storage mode is claimed.
The fiber project explicitly uses SliderV3 strain-driven plasticity as a perturbation.
The later nine-yard network reimplements angular sampling and phase-delayed departures with a multilayer routing graph.
Sol cites the original turntable's clock windows as conceptual ingredients of a separate structural-growth engine.
Claude uses the time-window problem from the single yard in a separate ant-like route-selection algorithm.
Sol cites AISol's multilevel yards but explicitly says its apical/basket/chandelier controls are not yet integrated.
Independent same-day growing-rail programs with different exploration/credit mechanisms; no file inheritance.

motifs.title: The receiver clock makes time a selective address
motifs.description: Track length, rotating input windows, complex-phase departure, pilot synchronization and time-dependent routing produce complementary but designed timing mechanisms. A biological neural analogy is not itself a physiological validation.

motifs.title: Rails can store which deliveries were useful
motifs.description: Two independent construction models reinforce ACK-winning routes under resource limits, cut pathways, retarget and expose lock-in. Their global budgets and path knowledge are not yet a completely local growth process.

motifs.title: Parameter nonidentifiability differs from a mirror-protected dynamical sector
motifs.description: Friday's mirror and TorsionFreeMirrorLock's port-indistinguishable interior are separate constructions. The latter has a privileged read key; usable local self-repair remains to be shown.

motifs.title: A spectacular representation may conceal a very small active loop
motifs.description: GeometricNeuronOriginReview proves an old PerceptionLab image feedback branch is an exact scalar lookup; the ordered window and four-tick host scheduler, not pixel count or unused integral state, set the behavior.
